origin.description: Alias of assertFunction. Returns the value when it is a function with the requested formals. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.usage: assert_function(x, args = NULL, ordered = FALSE, nargs = NULL, null.ok = FALSE, .var.name = vname(x), add = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: Formal argument names the function must have.

arguments.name: ordered
arguments.text: When true, classes or factor levels must be in this order.

arguments.name: nargs
arguments.text: Exact number of formal arguments, not counting ...

arguments.name: .var.name
arguments.text: Name used in the assertion message.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: Collection that stores the message instead of stopping.

origin.details: Alias of assertFunction. Returns the value when it is a function with the requested formals. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check stops.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(checkmate))
fn <- function(x) x
stopifnot(is.function(assert_function(fn, "x")) || isTRUE(assert_function(fn, "x")))
cat('function\n')

translation.details: Alias of assertFunction. Returns the value when it is a function with the requested formals. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
translation.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check raises CheckError.
translation.example:
from checkmate import *

def fn(x):
    return x

result = assert_function(fn, "x")
print('function' if callable(result) or result is True else result)
